gfc: jackpot £3200. £20 & harte, carrickmore, matthew dolan and teresa hoy, derrygonnelly. draw in doogies tonight. thanks to veryone who supports, promotes and supervises the lott o. condolence to the keown family on the recent passing of seamus keown, tullykelter. points to ponder to love the lord with all our heart – is this even possible? a common assumption is that love must just come, that it grows organically, and that it cannot be forced. that’s infatuation, not true love. any kind of love – for a parent, spouse, child, or friend – will reach a point during which it is no longer easy. for love to be true, it must be a free choice and commitment. ‘all your heart, soul, and mind’ sounds rather extreme, even rather dangerous. the world says that loving anyone totally is a risky proposition – what if the one we love rejects us or lets us down, leaving us with nothing? and the world is even more terrićed to love god totally, who cannot even be seen. this makes sense; after all, to love totally is to trust that we will ćnd fulćlment precisely by not looking for it ourselves, but by looking to fulćl someone else. that old, almost clichéd phrase, ‘love grows when it is given away,’ is actually spot-on in this regard. true love takes a leap of faith, which is what frightens nonbelievers. many people are okay with going to church every now and then or volunteering for a charity from time to time (and posting it on instagram, of course). loving like that does not require us to make any kind of leap, any kind of dećnitive change, any commitment. but loving god with everything means that all we do is for love of him. we trust that he will take care of us. that is heroic; that is what it means to be a saint. epriest.com morning reflection prayer for self-confidence heavenly father, thank you for the gift of a new day. as i begin this morning, help me to remember that my worth is found in you and not in the opinions of others or in my own doubts. fill my heart with confidence, not pride, but the quiet ass urance that i am created with purpose and loved without condition . help me to recognise the gifts you have placed within me and give me the courage to use them wisely. when fear or insecurity tries to take hold, remind me that i do not walk alone. strengthen my mind, guide my words, and help me face each challenge with faith rather than worry. teach me to believe in the person you are shaping me to become. may i carry myself with kindness, speak with confidence , and trust that your plans for me are good. today, let me walk with peace, knowing that i am enough because i am yours. amen. our lady of silence abbey

email: mcparishofïce@clogherparishes.ie emergency number / sick calls only : 083 09 72 683 love god and love your neighbour in today’s gospel (matthew 22:34 –40), jesus reminds us that the heart of our faith is sim-ple: to love god with all our heart, soul and mind, and to love our nei ghbour as ourselves. these two commandments are closely connected. we cannot truly love god w ithout al- lowing that love to shape how we treat others. a kind word, a listening ear, a helping hand, or a willingness to forgive can all become expressions of god’s love in our daily lives. sometimes we may think that living our faith requires great gestures or extraordi nary deeds. yet jesus reminds us that holiness is often found in the ordinary moments of everyday life, in the patience we show, the compassion we offer, and the care we extend to those around us. as we go about the week ahead, may we ask ourselves: can others recognise god’s love through the way i treat them? may we strive to make love the guiding principle of our words, our actions and our relation- ships, so that our homes and parish community may become places where god’s love is truly felt and shared. annual muckno parish draw 2026 –2027 our annual muckno parish draw is an important source of support for the and development of our parish, and i warmly encourage everyone to getin- volved by supporting the draw and purchasing tickets from our parish promoters . we continue to carry a significant parish debt of approximately €700,000, and the draw is essential in helping us meet our repayments and manage t his responsibility. in the coming months, we also hope to begin the extensio n of our parish graveyard. this is a very important project for our community, but the cost quoted for the work is substantial. i am deeply grateful to all who support our parish through the annu al draw and our weekly parish enve- lopes. every contribution, no matter how large or small, makes a real difference and helps us to provide for the needs of our parish, both now and into the future. your continued generosity, encouragement and support are greatly appreciated. by working together, we can continue to care for our parish and provide for the needs of our commu nity for generations to come. thank you sincerely for your ongoing kindness and generosity. god bless fr adi castleblayney / muckno (clontibret)

sunday 1st november is all saints day. it is a holy day of obligation. there is an envelope in your box towards the diocesan levy which every parish must contribute to. from 12.00 noon on 1st november until midnight on 2nd november all who have confessed, received holy communion and prayed for the pope's intentions (one our father and hail mary or any other prayer of one's choice) can gain one plenary indulgence by visiting a church or oratory and reciting one our father and the apostle's creed. the indulgence is applicable only to the souls of the departed. confession may be made at any time within the week preceding or the week following 2nd november. holy communion may be received on any day from 1st of november to the 8th november. the faithful who visit a cemetery and pray for the dead may gain a plenary indulgence applicable to the holy souls on the usual conditions once per day from 1st to the 8th november.
